source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 3 (ISL A3) · lesson 9. Rewritten for children from Dr. Hassan's lesson; facts and references kept.

learn.en: Zakāh is the third pillar of Islam. In Arabic it means purity and growth.
learn.title: Purity and growth

learn.en: Zakāh is a set share of wealth that a Muslim gives every year to people in need, once his wealth reaches a certain amount.
learn.title: A yearly share

learn.en: The Qur'an puts it next to prayer again and again: “Establish prayer and give zakāh.” (Qur'an 2:43)
learn.title: Always with prayer

learn.en: Zakāh cleans the giver's heart from greed, brings blessing into the money, helps the poor, and makes rich and poor love each other.
learn.title: Why is it purifying?

learn.en: Ṣadaqah is any giving, any time, any amount — even a smile! Zakāh is the part that is a must, with set rules.
learn.title: Zakāh or ṣadaqah?

quiz.en: What does the word zakāh mean?
Which pillar of Islam is zakāh?
True or false? Ṣadaqah can be given any time, any amount.
True or false? Zakāh makes the giver's heart greedy.

think.q: If you had some money of your own, who would you like to help with it?
think.a: Maybe a poor family, an orphan, or a neighbour in need — giving makes your heart clean and your money blessed.

parents.summary: Zakāh, the third pillar, is a yearly share of wealth for those in need. It purifies the heart and the money. Ṣadaqah is extra giving at any time.
parents.tip: Keep a family charity jar and let your child choose where it goes.
